subject.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout

question: Should LINE inbound media use an unconditional 120-second body wall-clock, accepting that slower valid transfers will fail closed?
rationale: Tests establish the mechanism, but repository precedent alone cannot determine whether LINE users should trade potentially slow valid delivery for a hard upper bound; that channel policy requires owner intent.

options.title: Accept the 120-second bound
options.body: Approve the separate 120-second body cutoff after redacted live LINE proof confirms an ordinary production download succeeds.

options.title: Revise the transfer policy
options.body: Choose a different bounded timeout or progress policy and add focused coverage for both wedged and slow-valid LINE transfers.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until maintainers have enough production data to choose a safe LINE transfer budget.

recommendation.title: Accept the 120-second bound
recommendation.body: Approve the separate 120-second body cutoff after redacted live LINE proof confirms an ordinary production download succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: He co-authored and merged the current LINE download implementation and is the strongest available owner for its compatibility policy.
